title: Exact finite-family Gaussian robust-testing oracle

candidate_glrt.score: T(x) = max_i log f_Ai(x) - max_j log f_Bj(x)

robust_p_value.validity: finite-family size control follows because p_sup >= p_k under every true null member B_k; this fixture also has an exact closed-form p-value

least_favourable_mixtures.least_favourable: The symmetric equal-weight mixtures are least-favourable for this two-point symmetric fixture. Their Neyman-Pearson rejection region is |x| <= r_alpha.
least_favourable_mixtures.maximin_proof: The Neyman-Pearson lemma upper-bounds average alternative power for every uniformly level-alpha test. The mixture-optimal test has equal size alpha at both null members and equal power at both alternative members, so its average power equals its worst-case power and it attains the maximin upper bound.
least_favourable_mixtures.scope: This is an exact oracle for this symmetric finite fixture only; it does not establish that equal weights, GLRT, or p_sup are maximin for arbitrary finite Gaussian families.

single_pair_robust_recalibration_baselin.interpretation: A single-pair rule remains uniformly size-controlled only after calibration against the least-favourable null member; it then has much poorer worst-case power than the exact symmetric minimax rule on this fixture. This is a constructed comparator, not a field-wide performance claim.

requirements: calibration draws are independent of the test observation
each component calibration stream is sampled from its exact declared null member
no threshold, score, nuisance bound, or family member is selected using sealed evaluation outcomes
monte_carlo_rank_contract.warning: A deterministic PRNG seed provides replayability, not physical randomness or an analytic proof.

proposed_qualification_targets.small_family_oracle_agreement: exact agreement in rejection ordering and agreement within 2e-6 for this normal-CDF approximation

validation.independent_numerical_replay: SciPy normal-CDF and root solution reproduced the frozen critical radius, size, and power values.
validation.rust: standalone reference and tests authored; rustc/Cargo unavailable in the authoring container, so compilation and execution were not performed

claim_boundary: This is an exact analytical minimax result for a one-dimensional symmetric two-point Gaussian family, paired with a standalone Rust reference using an approximate normal CDF. It is not a general composite-Gaussian minimax solver, a continuous-nuisance guarantee, a physical sensor validation, a CI pass, or evidence of SOTA superiority.
